tasks.title: Stream filter: extract a shared per-event renderer
tasks.description:
In `src/stream-filter.ts`, `processStream()` reads stream-json lines and renders them inline in its `for await` loop. Extract that per-event handling into a new exported function so the upcoming `cairn watch` command can render Claude Code subagent transcript lines with the same code.

Suggested signature: `export function renderEvent(e: Record<string, any>, opts: { truncateText: boolean }): string[]`. It returns zero or more rendered lines, without the `[#id] ` prefix and without trailing newlines. `processStream` keeps doing line splitting, JSON parse (non-JSON lines still pass through as-is), the prefix and the newline, and calls `renderEvent` for each parsed event.

Cover exactly the branches that exist today:
- `system`/`init` -> `  [init] model | mode`
- `assistant` content blocks: `tool_use` -> `  > fmtTool(...)`; `text`, with the existing truncateText first-line/80-char logic versus full multi-line output
- `result` -> `fmtResult`
- every other event type (including `type:"user"` tool_result events) -> `[]`

This is a PURE extraction. `processStream`'s output must be byte-for-byte unchanged, and `cairn run` (`src/commands/run.ts`, which calls `processStream` with `truncateText: config.truncateText`) must behave identically. Do NOT add tool_result rendering (decided in planning: `cairn watch` matches the old `-p` view, which never showed tool results).

Transcript lines Claude Code writes to `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` have the same shape as stream-json, e.g. `{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Read","input":{"file_path":"/a/b"}}]}}`. Unlike stream-json they never contain a final `result` event.

Tests (`test/stream-filter.test.ts`):
- Keep every existing `processStream` test green, unmodified.
- Add a `describe('renderEvent')` with cases for: an assistant `tool_use` block in transcript shape; an assistant `text` block with `truncateText` true and false (multi-line); a mixed content array; a `result` event; a `type:"user"` tool_result event (returns `[]`); and an unknown type (returns `[]`).

tasks.title: Transcript discovery module (src/transcripts.ts)
tasks.description:
Create `src/transcripts.ts`, a pure, read-only discovery module for Claude Code's subagent transcripts, used by the upcoming `cairn watch` command. It never writes anything.

Layout, established by probe (undocumented by Claude Code):
- Config dir is `process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude')`.
- Under it, `projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/subagents/` contains `agent-<id>.jsonl` (the live transcript) and `agent-<id>.meta.json`, e.g. `{"agentType":"post-task-reviewer","description":"Review #139",...}`.
- The slug is the absolute project root with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `-`. For example `/Users/jhummel/Documents/_Repos/cairn` -> `-Users-jhummel-Documents--Repos-cairn`.

Exports (names are suggestions):
- `projectSlug(projectRoot): string`.
- `claudeConfigDir(env = process.env): string`.
- `findSession(opts: { configDir, projectRoot, sessionId? })`:
  - Returns `{ ok: true, sessionDir }`, or `{ ok: true, sessionDir: null }` when the slug dir exists but no session has a `subagents/` dir yet (the caller waits quietly).
  - Returns `{ ok: false, error }` when `<configDir>/projects` or `<configDir>/projects/<slug>` is missing. The error message must name the exact path it looked for.
  - With no `sessionId`, pick the session whose `subagents/` dir has the newest mtime. With `sessionId`, use that session, and return a descriptive error naming the path if its `subagents/` dir doesn't exist.
- `listAgentTranscripts(sessionDir, { all?: boolean })`:
  - Returns `{ id, jsonlPath, metaPath, agentType, description, mtimeMs }[]`, sorted by `.jsonl` mtime, oldest first.
  - Parse `.meta.json` defensively: a missing or unparseable meta gives `agentType: undefined`, never throws.
  - Unless `all`, keep only `agentType` of `cairn-task-agent` or `post-task-reviewer` (filters out planning, Explore and general-purpose subagents). Export `DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPES` as a constant.

Use `fs` against real temp dirs. The config dir is passed in, so tests never touch the real `~/.claude`.

Tests (`test/transcripts.test.ts`, temp dirs with fixture `.jsonl` / `.meta.json` files and `fs.utimesSync` to control mtimes): slug derivation (including `_` and `.` -> `-`); `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` override versus the default; newest-session selection; explicit `sessionId`; no `subagents/` yet -> `sessionDir: null`; missing projects dir and missing slug dir -> error naming the path; filter versus `all`; missing or corrupt meta handled; sort order.

tasks.title: cairn watch command
tasks.description:
Add `cairn watch`, a live, full-detail view of the running `/cairn-run` subagent for a second local terminal. It replaces the live stream that headless `cairn run` showed. It is strictly READ-ONLY: it never touches run state, the hook, settle, `tasks.json` or `/cairn-run`.

Create `src/commands/watch.ts`. Register it in `src/index.ts` as `program.command('watch')` with options `--session <id>` (use this Claude Code session instead of the newest) and `--all` (show every subagent, not just `cairn-task-agent` / `post-task-reviewer`). It goes through the normal preAction (`setupProjectContext`), so the project root comes from `process.env.CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`. Use `loadConfig(projectRoot).truncateText` as the text truncation option, the same as `cairn run`.

Use task #144's `src/transcripts.ts` (`claudeConfigDir`, `findSession`, `listAgentTranscripts`) and task #143's `renderEvent` from `src/stream-filter.ts`.

Behavior: a poll loop at about 500ms. Do NOT use `fs.watch` (unreliable on macOS).
1. Startup. Resolve the session. On `{ok:false}`, print the error (it names the missing path) to stderr and exit 1 -- fail LOUDLY, never sit silently. If there is no session or no matching transcript yet, wait quietly and keep polling.
2. Replay. Take the newest matching transcript and replay it from byte 0, then follow it. Track a byte offset and read only appended bytes each poll. Buffer a trailing partial line until its newline arrives. JSON-parse each complete line; skip unparseable lines silently, never crash. Render with `renderEvent` and print each line plus newline.
3. Switching. On each poll, re-list transcripts, and re-resolve the newest session unless `--session` was given. When a NEWER matching transcript than the current one appears, first drain the current file to EOF, then switch, printing a header line `── <description> · <agentType> ──`, e.g. `── Task #143 · cairn-task-agent ──` (fall back to the agent id if there is no description). Print the same header before the initial replay.
4. Run until Ctrl-C.

Make it testable. Export a core function, e.g. `runWatch(opts, deps)`, where deps inject `sleep(ms)`, `write(text)`, `writeErr(text)`, the config dir, and a `shouldStop()` or max-iterations hook, so tests drive the loop with fake time and no real waiting. The Commander action wires in real defaults.

Tests (`test/commands/watch.test.ts`, temp-dir fake config dirs, never the real `~/.claude`):
- replay then follow: existing lines are rendered, then lines appended between polls are rendered exactly once
- a partial trailing line is held until complete
- an unparseable line is skipped
- switching: a newer matching transcript triggers drain-then-header-then-replay
- filter: an `Explore`/`general-purpose` agent is ignored by default and shown with `--all`
- missing projects or slug dir -> error naming the path, exit code 1
- no subagents yet -> no output, no error
- `--session` pins the session
Also add a check in `test/index.test.ts` (follow its existing pattern) that `watch` is registered with both options.

ROUND CONSTRAINTS: The binary is pinned for this round. Do NOT modify `cairn.json` (its `healthCheck` is deliberately pointed at `/tmp/cairn-healthcheck`), `install.sh`, or `package.json`'s `build` script, and do not run `./install.sh`. Never run `cairn round ...`, `cairn hook ...`, `cairn init` or `cairn watch` (or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init|watch ...`) against the project root; use temp dirs only. Use TDD: write the failing test first, see it fail, then make it pass.

tasks.title: Move the round bump from cairn plan to cairn round new
tasks.description:
Problem: `runPlan()` in `src/commands/plan.ts` calls `bumpRound(dataDir)` (from `src/task-counter.ts`) on every launch of `cairn plan`. A planning session that is quit and re-run therefore skips a round number (this round's `state.json` was found at 21 instead of 20). Fix: bump the round when the plan becomes tasks, via a new CLI command that `/generate-tasks` runs.

1. Remove the bump from `runPlan()`. Delete the `bumpRound(dataDir)` call and its import from `plan.ts`. In the same file, extend the planner's `--allowedTools` string from `'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent,Bash(cairn task next-id:*)'` to also include `Bash(cairn round new:*)`.

2. Add `cairn round new` in `src/commands/round.ts`, inside `registerRoundCommands`, next to `next` and `settle`. Use the same `loadRoundContext()` / `process.env.CAIRN_DATA_DIR`, and implement it as an exported, testable function such as `roundNewCommand({ dataDir }, deps)` that returns an exit code. It must:
- call `bumpRound(dataDir)`
- best-effort delete `<dataDir>/.cairn_planning_session.md` (the `/teach` learning-mode running log; build the name from `BRAND.tempPrefix` + `planning_session.md`). A missing file or a failed unlink is swallowed.
- print exactly one JSON object on stdout, like the other round commands: `{ "verdict": "round-started", "round": N, "next": "<one-line hint, e.g. that tasks.json can now be written and reviews go to reviews/round-N.md>" }`
- exit 0; exit 1 with one stderr line only if `state.json` can't be updated (e.g. lock timeout)
It lives under `round`, not `task`, for the same reason as `next`/`settle`: task agents only know `cairn task`, so they can't bump the round mid-round. Update the `registerRoundCommands` doc comment and the group description accordingly.

3. First-round semantics. In `bumpRound`, an ABSENT or non-finite round is now set to 1 (the first `/generate-tasks` in a fresh project starts round 1), while an existing numeric round is incremented. Update its doc comment and the existing `bumpRound` test '(e) seeds round: 2 when round is absent'. `getRound`'s 'absent means 1' read is unchanged. `bumpRound` has no other callers after step 1.

4. `commands/generate-tasks.md`. The approval step appears in two places: the RULES bullet 'Assign IDs to new tasks only after user approval...' (~line 149) and the final paragraph 'Once approved: (1) run `cairn task next-id`... (2) write `.cairn/tasks.json`...' (~line 159). In both, add running `cairn round new` once after `next-id`, before writing `tasks.json`, and say that its JSON reports the new round. State that it must be run ONCE per approved generation and NOT re-run when tasks are edited or regenerated in the same session, because each run bumps the round. That double-bump limitation is accepted and documented, not guarded.

Semantics note: during a planning discussion, `state.json` now shows the previous round. The only `getRound()` reader is `src/post-task-reviewer.ts`, at execution time, so it is unaffected.

Tests:
- `test/commands/plan.test.ts`: replace the tests 'bumps the planning round in state.json' and 'bumps the round even though spawnSyncFn is a stub' (~line 654) with tests asserting `runPlan` leaves `state.json`'s round unchanged, and that the spawned args' `--allowedTools` include `Bash(cairn round new:*)`.
- `test/commands/round.test.ts`, in temp dirs: `round new` increments an existing round; sets an absent round to 1; preserves `nextTaskId`; deletes `.cairn_planning_session.md` if present and succeeds if absent; prints exactly one valid JSON line with `verdict: 'round-started'` and the new round; returns exit code 0.
- `test/task-counter.test.ts`: the updated absent-round case.

ROUND CONSTRAINTS: The binary is pinned for this round. Do NOT modify `cairn.json` (its `healthCheck` is deliberately pointed at `/tmp/cairn-healthcheck`), `install.sh`, or `package.json`'s `build` script, and do not run `./install.sh`. tasks.title: Gitignore entries for /teach learning mode
tasks.description:
The upcoming `/teach` learning mode writes two personal files in the data dir. Both must be gitignored in every Cairn project:
- `.cairn/.cairn_planning_session.md`, a running scratch log of the planning session
- `.cairn/concepts.md`, a cumulative personal glossary

- Add `'planning_session.md'` to `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES`. `ignoreBlock(BRAND.tempPrefix)` turns it into `.cairn_planning_session.md`. Add a short comment that it is the `/teach` running log.
- Add `'concepts.md\n'` to `GITIGNORE_CONTENT`, alongside `instructions.md`, with a comment that it is the personal `/teach` glossary.

Re-init already merges missing `GITIGNORE_CONTENT` entries append-only via `currentGitignoreEntries()` and the merge function, so no merge code should change.

Note: `src/temp-sweep.ts` must NOT sweep either file, and doesn't by construction (its regexes require `task_<id>_`). Don't touch it. The running log must survive quitting a session.

tasks.title: /teach slash command (commands/teach.md)
tasks.description:
Write `commands/teach.md`, an opt-in, toggleable 'learning mode' planning style shipped with Cairn. `cairn init`'s `installMdDir` already copies every `commands/*.md` into a project's `.claude/commands/`. It is OFF by default; the user types `/teach` mid-session in `cairn plan` to turn it on.

Adapt the user's draft at `/Users/jhummel/Downloads/plan.md` ('Planning Session Mode', ~114 lines). Read it first; if it is unreadable, the spec below is complete. Keep the draft's voice: second person, addressed to the assistant, short sections. Give it frontmatter with a `description:` line like the draft.

KEEP from the draft:
- define terms on first use; explain the mechanism before naming it
- ask 'have you worked with X?' before assuming
- why -> mechanism -> recommendation
- one concept per message, concrete traces over abstractions, no walls of text
- the breadcrumb line `📍 Phase · Working on · Decided so far`
- end every reply with exactly one question or action
- name tangents and offer the way back
- understanding checks before locking a decision: one at a time, never self-answered, a plain correction if wrong
- steelman alternatives, name trade-offs, ask the failure question, separate requirement from preference, hold position without a new argument, flag scope creep
- don't challenge trivia

DROP: 'nothing gets implemented until let's build'. The Cairn planner never implements.

CHANGE:
1. Running log. Instead of the draft's `docs/PLANNING_STATE.md`, keep a gitignored scratch log at `.cairn/.cairn_planning_session.md`. Template sections: Goal; Current phase / focus; Decision log (table: #, decision, why, alternative rejected, open concerns); Open questions; Parked ideas; Next step. Update it as decisions land, with a one-line 'Logged decision #N' mention. `/generate-tasks` never reads it, and `cairn round new` deletes it when tasks are generated -- say so; the assistant must not delete it itself.
2. Re-entry briefing. On activation, if the running log exists, give a four-line briefing from it ('Where we are / Last decided / Open question / Suggested next step'); otherwise give it from `.cairn/planning-notes.md`. Then ask 'Does this match what you remember?'
3. Glossary `.cairn/concepts.md` (gitignored, personal, cumulative across rounds): read it at the start so known terms aren't re-explained; append terms as they're covered; when the user re-asks something already covered, point them to the entry.
4. `.cairn/planning-notes.md` rules are unchanged: it is written ONLY when the user says yes, in the planner's usual format, with Rejected Alternatives carried forward. The decision log may feed its Approach and Rejected Alternatives. State this explicitly.
5. 'Stopping' handoff. When the user says they're stopping, update the running log and give a three-line handoff.
6. Turning it off. `/teach off`, or 'back to normal mode', returns to the standard planner style. State that a later instruction overrides this one.
7. Compaction. If the style seems lost after compaction, re-run `/teach`.
8. Scope. Meant for `cairn plan` sessions, but harmless elsewhere.

The file must contain the literal paths `.cairn/.cairn_planning_session.md`, `.cairn/concepts.md` and `.cairn/planning-notes.md`. These must match task #147's gitignore entries and task #146's `cairn round new` deletion.

Optional, small: in `src/commands/plan.ts`'s `displayPreflight`, print one dim tip line such as `Tip: type /teach in the session for learning mode (explain-as-we-go).` If you add it, add a `test/commands/plan.test.ts` assertion.

Test (`test/commands/init.test.ts`, following the existing 'copies .md files from cairn commands/' tests near line 1306): running init into a temp dir installs `.claude/commands/teach.md`, and its content contains all three paths above. This guards existing copy behavior; no init code change is expected. Do not run `cairn init` against the project root.

tasks.title: Docs: cairn watch, cairn round new, /teach, round-bump semantics
tasks.description:
Document this round's features. Verify EVERY claim against the shipped code by reading the source, not this description. Change only `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`.

CLAUDE.md:
1. Command list under 'Execution flow': add a `watch` -> `src/commands/watch.ts` entry (read-only live view of the running `/cairn-run` subagent's transcript, `--session` and `--all`, replays the newest matching agent then follows, polls rather than `fs.watch`). Extend the `round` entry with `cairn round new`.
2. 'Two ways to run a round' / round verdicts: add the `round new` verdict (`round-started`, with `round` and `next`). It is run by `/generate-tasks` after `next-id`, and lives under `round` (not `task`) so task agents, which only know `cairn task`, can't bump the round mid-round. Note the CLI-owns-state principle: Markdown decides when, a tested command performs the state change. Document that it also deletes `.cairn_planning_session.md`.
3. `state.json` description, in the data layout and the 'Agent workflow' paragraph that says '`cairn plan` bumps the round counter on every planning run': correct it -- the round is bumped by `/generate-tasks` via `cairn round new`, not by `cairn plan` launches; an absent round becomes 1; during a planning discussion `state.json` shows the previous round; running `/generate-tasks` twice for one plan bumps twice (accepted, documented limitation).
4. Data layout tree: add `concepts.md` (personal `/teach` glossary, gitignored) and `.cairn_planning_session.md` (`/teach` running log, gitignored, deleted by `cairn round new`, never swept by temp-sweep). Add `teach.md` to the `.claude/commands/` example list.
5. A short note (in the watch entry or its own small subsection): `cairn watch` depends on Claude Code's UNDOCUMENTED subagent transcript layout -- `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (default `~/.claude`)`/projects/<slug>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` + `.meta.json`; the slug is the project root with non-alphanumerics -> `-`; it fails loudly naming the missing path if that layout changes; it renders assistant text and tool calls but not tool results (matching the old `cairn run` view) and no final Done line (transcripts lack a `result` event). Check the last two points against the actual code from tasks #143/#145.
6. A brief `/teach` mention: opt-in learning-mode planning style, off by default, toggled with `/teach` and `/teach off`; why it is a slash command and not `CLAUDE.local.md` (every session loads that, including task agents, which would stall waiting for confirmation) and not `planner.md` (`cairn init` overwrites it).

README.md:
- add `cairn watch` (usage, `--session`, `--all`, 'run it in a second terminal during `/cairn-run`') to the Commands section and the Execute workflow section
- add `/teach` to the Plan workflow section
